title: Rabbi Acha bar (Rav) Ulla (Illa, Ila)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman maintains that all these names are of one single Amora, and adduces this proof: in [Yerushalmi Eruvin 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.3.1.8), at the end of the halakhah, it states 'Rabbi Acha son of Rabbi Ila said that all things are called food'; and this statement appears in [Yerushalmi Nedarim 6:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Nedarim.6.1.3), as 'Rabbi Acha bar Ulla'; and in Bereshit Rabbah ch. 94, section 4 ([compare Bereshit Rabbah 94:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.94.2)), it is transmitted as 'Rabbi Acha bar Ilah'.

Hyman describes him as Rav Chisda’s student in Babylonia, citing [Shabbat 54b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.54b.11): 'He was sitting before Rav Chisda and he sat and spoke --' Rav Chisda said to him, 'If so, you have made [the sheep into] Mar Ukva!'.

Hyman says he later went to the Land of Israel, citing his exchange with Rabbi Zeira at the end of [Yerushalmi Eruvin 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.1.1.25), where he raised a difficulty against Rabbi Zeira, 'and why not'; and in [Yerushalmi Maaser Sheni 5:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Maaser_Sheni.5.3.7), 'Rabbi Yonah gave tithe to Rabbi Acha bar Ulla.'

He is mentioned in Tanchuma, Re'eh 12, where he asked, 'And is there Torah in the intestines?'; and in [Eruvin 21b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.21b.10), Rav Papa son of Rav Aya bar Adda said in his name, 'From where [do we know] that whoever mocks the words of the Sages is judged in boiling excrement'; and in [Shabbat 66a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.66a.14) he is mentioned under the name Rav Acha bar Rav Ulla.[^3]

notes.text: The fuller Shabbat 54b account concerns a freshly shorn sheep treated with oil; Rav Chisda’s comparison is to Mar Ukva.

Shabbat 54b directly names Acha bar Ulla before Chisda and compares the oil-treated, freshly shorn sheep to Mar Ukva. Hyman’s emphatic single-Amora argument, migration and Ulla/Illa/Ila name equations remain his; no authority records are merged.

The food passage names Acha son of Rabbi Ulla in the consulted Eruvin, Acha bar Ulla in Nedarim, and Rav Acha bar Ila in Bereshit Rabbah. The linked Bavli Eruvin has Papa son of Rav Acha bar Adda in the reporting chain, where Hyman gives Aya. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=325&lang=en) also collects the Ulla notices. The equation of all the forms and the migration narrative remain Hyman’s.
